claim: Documentation with exact computation, no theorem. The five four-place knot classes that prefer a value and exclude only two or three states (13-17) never failed on any 4-regular 4-uniform system examined: counterexample-guided SAT proves that no failing signing exists on every system it decided (all simple systems with n <= 7 and one with n = 8 for class 17; n <= 7 for 16; n <= 6 for 13 and 15; n = 5 for 14), and hill-climbing over signings keeps at least 2 solutions at n <= 9 and dozens to hundreds at n = 10, 12, 14, growing with n. A counting bound (n >= 16/|E|) makes failures impossible below n = 8 for 16 and 17 and below n = 6 for 13-15. A never-fails theorem is open.
conclusion: The five weak classes never failed in any search; whether they can fail at all is open.
